key_insight: KANs showed no systematic discrimination advantage over StandardMLP across datasets, although TabKAN and ReLUKAN improved AUPRC on severely imbalanced datasets.
clinical_relevance: KANs may merit evaluation for identifying rare positive cases in clinical tabular data, while StandardMLP remains a strong, efficient baseline.
method: Compared nine KAN variants, a tuned StandardMLP, and Random Forest across seven medical tabular datasets.
Used 3×5 repeated stratified cross-validation with nested Bayesian hyperparameter optimization.
Assessed AUPRC, Brier score, efficiency, and Bayesian equivalence with a ±0.01 ROPE.
evidence_signal: Across seven datasets spanning six clinical specialties, pooled discrimination was comparable, while KAN inference was 1.20–1.48× slower per sample and required up to 12.5× more trainable parameters.
watch_item: These cross-validation findings do not establish prospective clinical benefit, and KANs’ additional computational demands warrant consideration before deployment.
paper_title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. Multi-Layer Perceptrons: A Rigorous Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data
